question.prompt: According to the standard convention for exponentiation, \[2^{2^{2^{2}}}=2^{\left(2^{\left(2^{2}\right)}\right)}=2^{16}=65{,}536.\] If the order in which the exponentiations are performed is changed, how many other values are possible?

solutions.explanation:
Parentheses record which powers are evaluated first. To list every grouping, consider the final exponentiation: its base contains the first one, two, or three copies of \(2\), and its exponent contains the rest. A block of three copies has exactly two groupings, \((2^2)^2\) and \(2^{(2^2)}\). Thus the three cases give \(2+1+2=5\) groupings in total:
\[
\begin{aligned}
2^{(2^{(2^2)})}&=2^{16}=65{,}536,\\
2^{((2^2)^2)}&=2^{16}=65{,}536,\\
(2^2)^{(2^2)}&=4^4=256,\\
(2^{(2^2)})^2&=16^2=256,\\
((2^2)^2)^2&=16^2=256.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every grouping appears in exactly one of the three cases, according to how many copies of \(2\) are in its final base. The distinct values are therefore \(\{256,65{,}536\}\). Excluding the standard value leaves \(\boxed{1}\) other value, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: List all possible groupings
